supersedes.reason: Remediate independent-review findings F-001, F-002, and F-003 without rewriting the canonical plan or any version 1 raw result.

preservation.result_namespace: version 2 results are written only to an explicit output directory and never to a version 1 result path

measurement_gate.post_result_budget_or_tolerance_widening: forbidden; a failed sample remains failed

environment.postgres_lifecycle: each PostgreSQL sample runs the mission services.yaml postgres start, healthcheck, and stop commands
environment.network: not required; analyzer isolation records that plain subprocesses do not prove network denial

measurement_order: commit this successor plan before capturing any version 2 benchmark result
record the successor plan commit without changing any version 1 artifact, numeric budget, or tolerance
implement and test the F-001 accounting observer
implement F-002 and F-003 on commits descending from the successor plan commit
run each local sample in a fresh worker process group under an external descendant observer
for each PostgreSQL sample, start and healthcheck through services.yaml, observe the postgres container cgroup, and stop through services.yaml
write version 2 results only to an explicit non-version-1 output directory
verify and review raw version 2 results; preserve failures without widening budgets or tolerances

remediations.method: Replace coordinator resource.getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF) accounting with an external per-sample observer.

local_samples.isolation: launch one fresh Python worker with start_new_session=true, making the worker the leader of a new process group
local_samples.scope: aggregate resident bytes for the worker and the recursively discovered descendant closure on every snapshot
local_samples.descendants: include descendants even if they change process group; this includes Go compiler/runtime children and analyzer subprocesses
local_samples.coordinator: exclude the long-lived coordinator because it is neither the worker nor a descendant
local_samples.metric: maximum over time of the sum of resident bytes for all live members of the worker descendant closure
local_samples.hard_limit: terminate only the fresh worker process group if aggregate resident bytes exceed the unchanged case RSS budget

postgres_samples.isolation: start, healthcheck, and stop the postgres service for every sample through the supplied services.yaml lifecycle
postgres_samples.source: Docker container statistics backed by the postgres container cgroup
postgres_samples.scope: postgres container cgroup memory usage while the sample worker executes
postgres_samples.target: the exact container ID returned for the services.yaml postgres service
postgres_samples.metric: maximum observed postgres container cgroup resident-memory usage during the sample
postgres_samples.hard_limit: mark the sample failed if cgroup usage exceeds the unchanged case RSS budget; always stop through services.yaml

remediations.recomputation: within_budget is valid only when it equals peak_rss_bytes <= budget_bytes and budget_bytes equals hard_limit_bytes; parent-rusage, missing-source, non-isolated, or asserted-only accounting is rejected

remediations.method: Capture payload ciphertext independently immediately before and after rewrap.

precommit.before_capture: persist and read payload ciphertext through a distinct pre-rewrap capture
precommit.after_capture: read payload ciphertext again only after the new wrapped DEK and checkpoint exist
required_evidence: pre/post payload byte counts and SHA-256 digests
precommit.acceptance: recompute equal pre/post payload digests and lengths, unequal wrapped-DEK digests, exact generations, and checkpoint; never trust asserted unchanged booleans

remediations.method: Replace explicit ROLLBACK with an observed PostgreSQL backend disconnect.

precommit.fault: a unique client session inserts faulted decision and audit rows, emits an in-transaction readiness marker, then blocks without issuing ROLLBACK
precommit.injection: a separate control connection terminates that exact backend
precommit.verification: a fresh connection waits for backend disappearance and verifies automatic rollback
required_evidence: lost client connection and nonzero client exit
precommit.limitations: demonstrates backend-disconnect rollback only; process death, host crash, storage loss, WAL corruption, and fsync faults remain unproven

cases.comparison_method: Compare incremental SHA-256 and byte count with an independent whole-file SHA-256.
cases.acceptance_rule: All samples use 65536-byte bounded reads, preserve byte count, match the independent digest, and remain within both unchanged resource budgets.
limitations: The committed 2 MiB synthetic fixture is a bounded proof, not a 1 GiB release-load result.

cases.comparison_method: Write each source byte sequence to a new file and compare the exact readback bytes and aggregate SHA-256.
cases.acceptance_rule: Every one of at least six byte classes round-trips exactly in every sample within both unchanged resource budgets.
limitations: This prototype tests filesystem custody, not HTTP transfer framing.

cases.comparison_method: Instrument compression output before AES-GCM, decrypt then decompress, compare source digest, and mutate the authentication tag.
cases.acceptance_rule: Every sample proves compression precedes AEAD, exact readback succeeds, a one-bit ciphertext mutation fails, and both unchanged resource budgets hold.
limitations: The disposable deterministic nonce is safe only for this one-shot prototype and must not be copied into production.

cases.comparison_method: Create disposable PostgreSQL 17 partitions, insert bytea-only synthetic ciphertext, compare row/partition counts and inspect pruning and schema columns.
cases.acceptance_rule: All samples observe PostgreSQL 17 on port 5440, 200 rows, two partitions, no content plaintext column, pruning evidence, and both unchanged resource budgets.
limitations: The row count is a research proof, not production sizing guidance.

cases.comparison_method: Compare HMAC-SHA-256 equality tokens within and across organization, field, and generation scope.
cases.acceptance_rule: Same-scope equality matches; organization, field, and generation changes produce different fixed-length tokens within both unchanged resource budgets.
limitations: Equality and frequency leakage within a scope remains and is explicitly recorded.

inputs: old and new synthetic wrapping roots
cases.comparison_method: Independently capture payload ciphertext immediately before and after rewrap, then compare payload lengths/digests, old/new wrapped-DEK digests, generations, source identity, and checkpoint.
cases.acceptance_rule: Independently captured pre/post payload lengths and digests match, wrapped-DEK digests differ, generations and checkpoint match the precommit, and every sample stays within both unchanged resource budgets.
limitations: No cloud KMS call is made; provider conformance remains later work.

inputs: one blocked in-transaction client terminated by a separate PostgreSQL control connection
cases.comparison_method: Commit one complete triplet, terminate the exact backend of a second blocked in-transaction client without explicit rollback, then verify disappearance and automatic rollback from a fresh connection.
cases.acceptance_rule: Every sample has exactly one committed decision, audit, and receipt, acknowledged backend termination, a lost fault client with nonzero exit, backend disappearance, no faulted or orphaned row, PostgreSQL 17 on 5440, and both unchanged resource budgets.
limitations: Only backend-disconnect rollback is demonstrated; process death, host crash, storage loss, WAL corruption, and fsync faults remain unproven.

cases.comparison_method: Inspect child-visible environment, directory, descriptor limit, output size, and timeout while explicitly testing whether network denial is proven.
cases.acceptance_rule: Resource and ambient-state bounds hold, the external observer includes analyzer descendants, and acceptance requires the honest conclusion that a plain subprocess does not prove network denial.
limitations: This negative result rejects plain subprocess isolation as the complete hostile-extension boundary.

inputs: one late event and superseding replay
cases.comparison_method: Digest ordered immutable snapshots in PostgreSQL, repeat the pinned snapshot, add a late event, and append a superseding run.
cases.acceptance_rule: Recorded replay digests match, late replay differs, all three runs remain, PostgreSQL 17 on 5440, and both unchanged resource budgets hold.
limitations: Tenant fairness and crash recovery need larger production-stage fault tests.
